tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Copland and British Orchestral Music

questions.question: Describe how copland and british orchestral music are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary.
questions.correctAnswer: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their effect.

questions.question: Compare how two different pieces use copland and british orchestral music. Explain the effect in each case.
questions.correctAnswer: A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how copland and british orchestral music are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative language.

questions.question: How could you use copland and british orchestral music in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
questions.correctAnswer: A practical application showing understanding of how copland and british orchestral music can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

tests.name: Extended Practice
tests.description: Self-marked extended answers on Copland and British Orchestral Music

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Compare Copland's orchestral style with a British composer from this area of study. Identify at least three musical features that distinguish each composer's approach. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: identify Copland's specific techniques (open harmony, folk melody, sparse texture); name British composers and their distinctive features; explain how each composer's style reflects their cultural context; use precise analytical vocabulary. Mark scheme: AO3 (analyse and evaluate) + AO4 (knowledge and understanding) = total marks for listening; AO1 (perform) + AO2 (compose) for coursework components
questions.explanation: Extended answer: aim for the mark-scheme points, in order, with the command word addressed.
